approach: Root cause: after a squash the host's commit is not a descendant of the job's landed commit. `resync_tip` (land.rs:218) repairs that with `git.replay`, which rebuilds every later commit under new ids. The branch leaves its remote copy's history, so a plain push is refused, and the drain never pushes. Change: (1) `resync_tip` builds a merge commit with parents [head, merged] instead of replaying. It takes the tree from `git.merge_tree(landed, head, merged)` and commits it with `git.commit_tree`. Before committing it requires the merge to leave the branch's governed fingerprint unchanged. In the normal case the host's squash tree equals the landed tree, so the merge tree equals head's tree and the existing `classify_pre_merge` rule 4 already classes the merge as records-only; no gate change is needed. Any other case (conflict, or governed content the branch lacks) is an error and nothing moves. (2) `Athena::push_working_branch` does a plain push of the current branch through `GitRemote`. `after_merge` calls it after the resync, which covers `athena land --pr` and the drain's `PrLander`. The drain also gets a defaulted `Steps::push_after_landing` hook that `Drain::land` calls after each `Landed` result and that `RealSteps` implements with the same helper. (3) Landing records and intents skip commits already named by an earlier landing record, so the append-only branch does not list landed jobs again. The gate (invariant.rs, history.rs, pr_check.rs) is not changed.

decisions.choice: Do not change the gate. resync_tip itself refuses any merge whose governed fingerprint differs from head's (`fingerprint(git, &tree, head) != fingerprint(git, head, head)`), naming the first differing path; the branch is unchanged. Answers critic finding 5, scope findings 1 and 2, and finding 8.
decisions.reason: land_pr pushes the landed commit as the PR head (landing.rs:892-905) and main must be up to date before merging (System facts), so the squash tree equals the landed tree and merge_tree(landed, head, merged) returns head's tree. classify_pre_merge (invariant.rs:339-347) then gives RecordsOnly by rule 4 with no edit, and the commit adds nothing a parent does not hold. A looser 'verbatim from any parent' rule would let a merge with an ancestor as second parent revert governed content as RecordsOnly. Because resync_tip only creates merges whose governed content equals the first parent's, it cannot create such a revert. A hand-made revert merge stays GovernedChange, and a test shows it.

rejected.option: Add `merge_paths_not_taken` as a new first rule of classify_pre_merge
rejected.why: A second parent that is an ancestor of the first lets a merge revert governed content and still pass as RecordsOnly. It also widens scope to invariant.rs and landing_tests.rs for a case the host's up-to-date rule rules out.

rejected.option: Tighten the gate rule to a one-sided merge (second parent's content, first parent unchanged since the merge base)
rejected.why: More gate code and tests in files outside the request, to support only the case where main moved while the up-to-date rule was off. A refusal with the branch unchanged is the smaller design.

rejected.option: Keep replay for the case where main carries other governed content
rejected.why: The replay is the rewrite the request removes; it would leave the divergence bug in that path.

decisions.choice: Build the merge tree with merge_tree(base = landed, ours = head, theirs = merged), commit it with commit_tree(parents [head, merged]) and move the branch with the existing reset_keep.
decisions.reason: A plain `git merge` uses the real merge base and conflicts whenever a later job edits lines the landed job added; with the landed commit as base only the host's changes beyond the landed job come in. merge_tree, commit_tree (athena-git lib.rs:612, takes &[&str] parents and a sign flag) and reset_keep (lib.rs:759) exist, keep local edits and follow signs_commits.

rejected.option: git merge in the work tree
rejected.why: Conflicts on later edits of landed lines, can leave a half-done merge, and bypasses signing and the keep-edits behavior.

rejected.option: Keep replay and force-push or push_if_remote_at
rejected.why: Out of scope and rejected by the request; it treats the symptom.

decisions.choice: Exclude already-landed commits from landing intents and landing records using the landing records, in gh/records.rs: for each landing record whose host_commit is an ancestor of the expected base, pass its head_sha as `^head_sha` to a new `land::pr_commits_excluding`. pr_commits calls it with no exclusions. Keeps records.rs in scope (finding 3).
decisions.reason: Under append-only, old landing commits stay in expected_base..head. throughput.rs:391-402 takes the newest landing record that holds a job's JobLanding commit as that job's landing time, so listing a landed job again moves its landing time, and the new intent would name old jobs. Landing records already hold head_sha and host_commit (athena-data/src/history.rs). The rule is that messages are never read (land.rs:245-246), so a message marker is out. The landing head contains everything the squash held, so ^head_sha is exact.

rejected.option: A marker line in the merge message
rejected.why: Free text deciding what is judged.

rejected.option: Exclude commits reachable from the first parent of any merge whose second parent is on the base
rejected.why: Anyone could hide a whole branch history by making such a merge.
Double counts JobLanding commits and moves landing times.

decisions.choice: Push from two places through one helper: `after_merge` (covers athena land --pr and PrLander) and a defaulted `Steps::push_after_landing` that Drain::land calls after a `Landed` result and RealSteps implements. A real drain therefore runs the helper twice per landing; the second call is one ls-remote that finds the remote already at head and is silent. A refused push warns from both calls.
decisions.reason: The drain test seam needs the hook: tests/drain.rs runs RealSteps with a fake Lander that never reaches after_merge, so only the hook can show the drain pushing. athena land --pr needs the real gh, so only after_merge can be tested for it. The helper reads head once and pushes that explicit commit. I chose to accept the extra ls-remote and possible repeated warning rather than add state; it is stated in risks (critic finding 7).

rejected.option: Remember the last pushed head inside Athena so the second call is skipped
rejected.why: Needs a new field with interior mutability on a core type for one saved ls-remote.

rejected.option: A Lander method so PrLander skips the hook
rejected.why: A landing confirmed without reaching after_merge would not push; the hook is the safer owner of the drain's push.
A drain test would need push logic in a double.

rejected.option: Push only in commands::land and RealSteps::land
rejected.why: commands::land needs the real gh, so no test could show it.
Every Steps double in drain.rs, tests/drain.rs, job_plan.rs and focus.rs would change.

decisions.choice: The drain test that proves the push drives RealSteps (athena-cli/tests/drain.rs) with a fake Lander (RecordingLander pattern, line 2289) on a fixture with a bare origin. A Stub test in drain.rs checks only the order and the not-landed case.
decisions.reason: A Stub that records a string cannot show that RealSteps::push_after_landing is wired or that anything reaches a remote (critic finding 6). With RealSteps the origin's branch is read after each landing.

rejected.why: Passes even if the RealSteps override is empty.

decisions.choice: A failed or refused push is a warning line; no origin, a detached HEAD or no commit is a silent skip; the push is GitRemote::push (git push, no force option, gh/remote.rs:10 and :52), never forced.
decisions.reason: The merge is already done on the host, so a refused push must not undo it or trigger a drain retry. Many drain fixtures have no origin and would otherwise warn on every landing.

rejected.option: Return the push error from after_merge or the drain
rejected.why: Turns a finished landing into a failure.

decisions.choice: Move the two fixtures that resync a checkout that is main itself (test_support.rs:559, trailer_stop.rs:131) to reset_keep.
decisions.reason: Attribution walks main's first-parent line from C0 (attribution.rs:386-409); a merge on a branch named main would put C0 off it. Nothing followed the landed commit there, so the old replay result equals reset_keep.

rejected.why: athena check --attribution on the fixture would report the cutover commit off main's first-parent line.

decisions.choice: Leave Git::replay, athena-git/src/lib.rs and gh/mod.rs untouched; they are listed as deliverables but need no change.
decisions.reason: replay stays public with its own tests (lib.rs:1659-1724), so no dead-code warning; removing it is a separate clean-up. gh/mod.rs only declares modules, and the new tests sit in the existing test modules.

decisions.choice: Keep gh/records.rs and gh/after_merge_tests.rs in scope (findings 3 and 4) and ask the user. Drop invariant.rs and landing_tests.rs (findings 1 and 2).
decisions.reason: records.rs is the only place landing records choose a pull request's commits, and without it landed jobs are listed again. after_merge_tests.rs:103 asserts the old text `rebuilt on the merged commit`, which would be false after the change; it is a one-line needle change. The two gate files are no longer needed.

rejected.why: Landed jobs would be listed in every later landing record, and an existing test would fail on the new message.

rejected.option: Keep the old message text so after_merge_tests.rs stays unedited
rejected.why: The branch is no longer rebuilt; the text would be false.

risks.risk: Append-only growth: squashed landing commits never become reachable from main, so every later head's own-commit range grows by each landing, and the CI history check and check_pr_head classify all of them each run.
risks.mitigation: Each old landing commit is a valid job landing and each resync merge classifies as records only, so the checks pass; landing intents and records stay short through the record-based exclusion. A few extra git calls per commit; a follow-up can apply the exclusion in history.rs and pr_check.rs. The CHANGELOG states the growth; per-job branches (D167) are the long-term answer.

risks.risk: resync_tip is stricter than the replay: governed content the host's commit carries and the branch lacks, or a file changed on both sides, is an error where the replay carried on.
risks.mitigation: The error names the first differing path and the branch is unchanged, as for a conflict; the maintainer merges by hand. The host requires main to be up to date, so the normal case gives a tree equal to the head's. Tested as case (d) of criterion 4.

risks.risk: Double push attempt per landing in a real drain (critic finding 7).
risks.mitigation: A real drain runs the push helper twice per landing (after_merge, then the hook). The second call is one ls-remote under the landing lock and is silent when the remote holds head. A refused push shows the warning twice. This is accepted, not hidden; the hook is needed for the drain test seam.

risks.risk: The push is refused or origin is unreachable.
risks.mitigation: A warning line gives the reason; the landing and local resync stand. The first landing after this change may be refused once if the remote copy was force-pushed by hand earlier; the next landing pushes the whole append-only history with a plain push once the maintainer reconciles the remote.

risks.risk: Existing tests assume the rewritten shape (text needle, linear branch, main == C0).
risks.mitigation: The dependents list names each: the after_merge needle, the two land.rs resync tests and the two fixtures. The full suite and the per-crate runs in criterion 6 cover the rest.

risks.risk: The tests/drain.rs fake-agent fixture may not support two queued requests with one scenario script.
risks.mitigation: If the scenario script cannot work two queued requests, the tests/drain.rs test lands one job and checks the origin after it, and the Stub test still shows one push per landing for two jobs; the producer reports this rather than weakening the assertion.

risks.risk: A slow ls-remote or push inside the drain's landing lock.
risks.mitigation: One git call per landing, with the same network exposure as the landing's own pushes; it holds no records or job state, and a failure is only a warning.

risks.risk: docs/design/native-pr-landing.md section 5.2a and D88 still describe the replay.
risks.mitigation: Named in open questions and the CHANGELOG entry; the code comments and new tests carry the behavior.

It asserts: at the second ask the origin's main contains the head recorded at the first ask (pushed after landing 1); after the drain the origin's main contains the second landing's head and is an ancestor of the local head (only fast-forwards, no divergence); report.landed == 2. (c) A second tests/drain.rs test: the origin first receives a sibling commit made with `git commit-tree` on the fixture's base commit (a plain push to the empty bare repo, so the origin's main diverges from the job commits without any force in the test). The drain run shows `report.landed == 1`, the job's landing text is `landed`, the origin's main is unchanged (a force would have replaced it), and a captured Ui line starts with `warning: could not push`. Core tests of Athena::push_working_branch: a bare origin is pushed once and the second call is silent; an origin at a missing path warns and returns false; no origin and a detached HEAD are silent.
